digest.component_or_area: plan-review gate - impact model and verifier
propositions: The divergent_implementation axis fires on only 7.72% of plan-v3 findings despite being a hard-override axis, and ~90% of the omitted-scope-site class is graded none despite being the axis's primary purpose.

A G6 finding (validity 0.8889, impact 0.0, ADVISORY despite blocking_enabled=true) represents a real plan divergence that should block but does not because all seven impact axes were graded none under the current ordinal ladder.

The new three-grade Literal (contradicts_reality, omits_required_site, incomplete_enumeration) replaces the retired ordinal ladder for divergent_implementation, with the first two flooring at 0.85 and the third contributing below every blocking threshold to serve as a pressure-release valve.

ADR-0054 rejects high-cost LLM-based calibration (purpose-built eval suites, bulk re-review runs) and restricts A/B testing to zero-marginal-cost corpus replay and dogfooding, narrowing but not superseding ADR-0036's permissive-rollout invariant.

Rejecting the prod_impact floor (Fix 2) as proposed because it would lift unbounded severity findings across the novelty convergence floor, enabling non-terminating remediation loops unlike Fix 1's semantically-bounded divergence class.

The corpus-replay pre-landing bound shows worst-case addition of 81 blocks across 1,396 findings graded non-none on divergent_implementation—a bounded increase well below the 113-block over-fire that an ungraded widening would produce.
